title: Which fraction of the square is shaded?
description: The video finds four products of two fractions with one on top, and then one twelfth times one eighteenth, by counting the rows times the columns in a unit square, the same way as the example in the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: the rows times the columns give all the equal parts of the unit square, and one part is shaded, so the product is one over the product of the bottoms. Watch for students who add the bottoms.

video_script.why: The child has found a fraction of a fraction by cutting a unit square and now does the same for four products, and then for a product too big to draw easily.
video_script.substitution: The rows times the columns count all the equal parts of the square, and one part is shaded.
video_script.anchor: Four products of two fractions with one on top, then one twelfth times one eighteenth
video_script.payoff_line: One twelfth times one eighteenth is one two hundred sixteenth

final_answer.spoken: one fifteenth, one twelfth, one tenth, one thirtieth, and one two hundred sixteenth

video_script.fraction_reading: one third, one fifth, one quarter, one half, one sixth, one twelfth, one eighteenth, one fifteenth, one tenth, one thirtieth, one two hundred sixteenth
maths_rules: 1/3 × 1/5: 5 rows and 3 columns, 5 × 3 = 15 equal parts, 1 shaded, 1/15
1/4 × 1/3: 3 rows and 4 columns, 3 × 4 = 12 equal parts, 1 shaded, 1/12
1/5 × 1/2: 2 rows and 5 columns, 2 × 5 = 10 equal parts, 1 shaded, 1/10
1/6 × 1/5: 5 rows and 6 columns, 5 × 6 = 30 equal parts, 1 shaded, 1/30
1/12 × 1/18: 18 rows and 12 columns, 18 × 12 = 216 equal parts, 1 shaded, 1/216
video_script.design: One idea: the rows times the columns count all the equal parts, and one part is shaded. A unit square cut into rows and columns is the anchor and stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>Step one, start with one third times one fifth.
Do it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>The square has five rows and three columns, so five times three makes fifteen equal parts. One part is shaded.
<bookmark mark='b1'/>Next, one quarter times one third has three rows and four columns.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>That makes twelve equal parts, with one part shaded.

<bookmark mark='parts'/>The number of equal parts is the first bottom times the second bottom.

<bookmark mark='prod'/>Eighteen times twelve makes two hundred sixteen equal parts, with one part shaded.
